 Julian Hall officially cap-tied to USMNT with Nations League appearance
 November 14, 2026 by Larry Henry Jr 
 Dual-national forward Julian Hall is officially cap-tied to the U.S. Men’s National Team.
 Hall sealed the deal with his start on Saturday against Haiti in CONCACAF Nations League play. The 18-year-old Hall entered the match needing one competitive start to meet FIFA’s requirements and got the starting nod from head coach Mauricio Pochettino. 
 It marked Hall’s fifth senior cap for the USMNT since debuting during the September-October window. 
 Hall scored in previous friendlies against Peru, Chile, and Mexico, while also appearing in a home victory over Canada last month. 
 The New York Red Bulls forward was eligible to represent Poland, in addition to the USMNT, but is now officially tied to the United States. 
 Hall enjoyed a breakout MLS season this year, scoring 16 goals in 35 appearances for the Red Bulls. Despite his best efforts, Michael Bradley’s squad failed to make the postseason by four points. 
 Hall remains a top attacking option for the USMNT going forward into the next World Cup cycle.
